input: I pull on my coat, fasten the Garvey signet, and open the door. "I was hoping soup might be the part I understood. Rowan, by the way." I give my visitor a small, embarrassed smile and head toward the dinner with them, taking a moment at the doorway to see who is already there.
output:
Ashara vel Kothren waits in the doorway, tall enough that the landing seems built around her rather than for her. Her swept-back horns are black-red in the lamplight; heat rolls softly from her dark formal jacket. Gold slit pupils flick over the signet, then the ink on your fingers.

“Ashara vel Kothren,” she says. “And soup is one of the Academy’s less political inventions.” Her tail gives a brief, impatient curve. “Come before Rashid decides lateness is an opening position.”

She takes the stairs at a pace that assumes you will keep up, though not one meant to lose you. The dining hall below glows with working lamps and thin candlelight, its huge varnished table absurdly long for the cluster of students gathered at one end. Servers in blue-and-silver livery set covered dishes down with the solemnity of priests.

“—current ranking, not permanent rank,” Ashara is saying as you cross the threshold.

The wolf-blooded man opposite her smooths a cuff over dark fur. “A distinction you find comforting.” He rises, amber-eyed and impeccably dressed. “Rashid vel Amara. Welcome, Rowan.”

Place cards offer the rest before anyone can: YSOLDE THORNMANTLE beside a still white-haired woman watching stormlight through the windows; CAELINDRA VAEYN before a pale-gold elf whose violet gaze takes inventory and gives nothing back; THESSALY MORROW beside a small woman with black eyes and a smile arriving a beat late. At the far end sit two angels in white and gold: Aldric, upright even before dinner, and Seraphel Dawnquill, whose folded little wings shine at their edges.

Seraphel looks up.

“New chair, new bread, a stranger at the board—  
May kindness come before a sharpened word.”

Caelindra’s pointed ear tips toward her. “That is either kind or threatening.”

“Both may be true,” Thessaly says.

Ashara gestures to the card marked ROWAN GARVEY, set between Thessaly and Ysolde. Aldric rises, hand to his breast.

“Before we eat, we offer thanks for safe arrival,” he says. “You may join us, Rowan, or keep your seat. I would rather ask than presume.”
